summary: End-to-end UI verification of the five new IVR key actions (webhook, collect digits, PIN, pay-link, submenu) plus 3-level sub-menu nesting on +13346970100 for civr.alice@example.com. Every requested flow passes through real Save + reload in the browser. (1) Webhook key: https://example.com/hook saves, persists after reload, shows success toast. http://example.com/x rejected with toast 'Key 3: enter a web address that starts with https://' and NOT saved. https://127.0.0.1/x rejected with 'Key 3: that address leads to a private or internal network — use a public https:// address.' (2) Collect digits: with prompt='Enter your order number', length=8, message='Thanks for your order number' saves + persists. Empty prompt rejected with 'Key 3: say what the caller should type.' (3) PIN: pin=4821 + forward=+14155550100 saves + persists. Pin='4' rejected with 'Key 3: the PIN needs at least 3 digits.' (4) Pay-link: payUrl=https://buy.stripe.com/test_abc + payNote='Pay here:' saves + persists; sms-from picker shows '+12025550111 · Texting Number' (id mn_ab01) and NO smsText/smsVersions free-text editor is rendered (hideText works). Call flow tree renders 'Key 3 · Text a payment link · https://buy.stripe.com/test_abc'. (5) 3-level sub-menus: nested submenu → submenu → submenu → message(leaf 'Deepest leaf message') saves + reloads. At L4 (depth 3) the action dropdown options are exactly [forward, message, sms, voicemail, webhook, collect, pin, pay] — 'submenu' correctly omitted. Call flow tree shows all four nested levels. (6) Checks panel: 'Key 3 — Add the secure https web address (webhook URL) this key should call.' / 'Add at least one PIN code...' / 'Add the https address of your own payment page...' appear for empty new keys and clear to 'Ready to save' when fixed. 'Test my menu' returned '6 passed' including a row 'Key 3 · press 3 → texts the caller your payment link, then hangs up'. (7) Emily (chat mode): when asked 'Add a key 5 that lets callers type their order number and sends it to https://example.com/orders, and a key 6 that texts my payment link https://buy.stripe.com/test_abc', her proposal correctly contains both URLs. Clicking ivr-assist-apply populated the builder: Key 5 action=collect, collect-webhook=https://example.com/orders, prompt filled; Key 6 action=pay, pay-url=https://buy.stripe.com/test_abc, pay-note filled; greeting updated to mention keys 5 and 6. When asked 'Add a key that calls my system' with no URL, she asked a clarifying question and did NOT invent a URL. Regression: forward (key 1) and sms (key 2) still save and reload intact. Restore: the menu was restored exactly to the baseline (greeting 'Press 1 for orders, press 2 for our menu by text.', Key 1=Forward +14155550100 label 'Orders', Key 2=SMS label 'Menu' from mn_ab01 with smsText 'Menu: bella.com/menu') and saved. Checks show 'Ready to save · No problems found.' IVR enable toggle was never flipped on.
action_items: (Nice-to-have) Emily: 'Add a key that calls my system' was interpreted as a forward key (she asked 'the phone number to forward the call to'). The user's wording 'calls my system' typically implies a webhook — consider updating the intent/prompt so webhook is suggested (and the URL is asked for) when the user says 'call / calls my system / my API / my server'. She did correctly refuse to invent a URL, which is the key invariant.
critical_code_review_comments: IvrTab.js ActionFields for the 'pay' branch renders <IvrSms ... hideText /> which also hides the 'Say after sending' line and the 'Then' picker inside IvrSms. The requirements only hide the free-text SMS editor, not the 'say after' message. Current behaviour is defensible (the caller is auto-told to check their text) but the hideText flag is now conflating two things — consider separating hideText vs hideVersions for clarity, or at least leave a comment.

IvrSms.js useEffect auto-picks the first texting number as smsFrom when the current selection is unknown — fine, but it fires on every mount of IvrSms, so switching a key from 'pay' back to 'sms' triggers another set() that marks the form dirty even though the user didn't change anything. Consider gating on !o.smsFrom.

IvrTab.js ACTIONS filter `depth < 3 || a !== 'submenu'` is equivalent to depth<3 for the submenu option. Works correctly but the double-negative reads awkwardly — rename to `(a !== 'submenu' || depth < 3)` for readability.

ivr-flow-checks greeting warn 'The greeting doesn't mention key 3 — callers won't know to press it.' uses the English literal; needs i18n if the UI language switches — currently fine because the whole backend validate response is English.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Save-error toasts are rendered by sonner at <li data-sonner-toast>; query THAT (not generic .toast / class*=error) to read them. Nested add-key testids follow a strict recursive pattern: ivr-add-option-button (top), ivr-option-<i>-sub-add-option-button (L2 list add), ivr-option-<i>-sub-option-<j>-sub-add-option-button (L3 list add), etc. Row testids mirror this: ivr-option-<i>-sub-option-<j>-sub-option-<k>-{action-select,digit-select,label-input,<field>}. L4 (depth 3) correctly filters 'submenu' out of the action dropdown. Emily proposal apply control is data-testid='ivr-assist-apply' (not suffixed by message index as the prior iteration guessed) and the proposal block testids are ivr-assist-proposal-<msgIdx>-{summary,missing}. The Call flow blueprint uses a 400ms debounce on edits, so always wait_for_timeout(1500+) before reading [data-testid=ivr-flow-checks] / ivr-flow-tree after a change.
rca of the issue: No defect reproduced on any of the five new key types. Save route accepts all of them, reload shows persisted values, error path returns clear per-key messages via sonner toasts. The only improvement is a prompt nit: Emily interprets 'calls my system' as forward, not webhook.
